device.model: KR 16-2 on a KR C4 controller (KUKAVARPROXY)
device.name: KUKA KR 16-2 via KUKAVARPROXY (KUKAVARPROXY_communication.KUKA)

facts.text: The module is a KUKAVARPROXY communication module used by opcua-server-xml.py for a KUKA KR C4 robot controller
KUKA is the module's device class and its constructor connects the module socket to TCP port 7000, where KukaVarProxy listens
The module builds the KukaVarProxy frame from a message id, a message length, a read/write byte, a variable name and an optional value
read(var) reads one KRL variable and write(var, val) writes one through the same KVP socket
The upstream reader reads $AXIS_ACT, removes the commas and splits the text on spaces, taking the value token after each axis name
The upstream control server writes TARGET_AXIS as an E6AXIS string with A1 to A6 entries
The KRL program initializes TARGET_AXIS from $AXIS_ACT and then loops PTP to TARGET_AXIS
The KRL program declares a global interrupt that calls the controller's IR_STOPM when $STOPMESS is true
The upstream velocity plotter reads each axis with $VEL_AXIS_ACT [n]
The upstream torque plotter reads each axis with $TORQUE_AXIS_ACT [n]
The upstream current plotter reads each axis with $CURR_ACT [n]
The upstream temperature plotter reads each axis with $MOT_TEMP [n] and subtracts an offset supplied to that script
The upstream error handler closes the socket and raises SystemExit on a network or parsing error; the driver converts that process-level exit into a normal failed receipt
The KUKA KR 16-2 object XML defines the six axis variables A1 to A6 and an IP property

operator_required.reason: the clone states no travel range for the KUKA axes: it reads and writes the native $AXIS_ACT / TARGET_AXIS values without a limit; the site supplies the travel envelope of the installed robot

safe_state.description: KRL target set to the last read axis position so the loop's next PTP target is where the arm was; the controller's $STOPMESS interrupt runs IR_STOPM independently of this driver
